notes: This minor release depends exactly on bifrost.public.packs 0.17.0. Its catalog loads on Bifrost 0.15.3 and later, and it was qualified on released Bifrost 0.15.4. New default policies: bifrost.security.python.predictable-temporary-path (bifrost.security 3.4.0, #96), and bifrost.correctness.python-numpy-global-rng-with-local-generator, python-or-default-argument-mutation, python-pandas-chained-inplace, python-pandas-inplace-result-used, python-shared-class-attribute-mutation and python-split-file-extension (bifrost.code-smells 4.1.0, #449-#458). New opt-in policies: bifrost.correctness.python-assert-argument-validation; bifrost.security.python.requests-, httpx-, aiohttp- and urllib3-tls-verification-disabled (#427, CWE-295); python.flask-request-in-assert, python.flask-request-to-decompress and python.flask-request-to-parse-qs (#433-#443); javascript.file-content-to-unbounded-decompression and javascript.process-input-to-fetch-url; and the candidate rust.cleartext-logging (#94, CWE-312). Limitation: the TLS-verification, flask-request-to-decompress, flask-request-to-parse-qs, both JavaScript and the Rust policies need source-only packs (Python HTTP-client and untrusted-parsing, Node zlib and fs, web-network JavaScript, Rust core-logging) that are not in packs 0.17.0, so with the released packs alone they do not report those flows and the run is not clean; a project can supply the models under .bifrost/semantic-models. bifrost.security.python.flask-request-to-urlopen and django-request-to-urlopen stay opt-in. packs 0.17.0 now ships their Flask, Werkzeug and Django models, but running them by default needs an engine that reports a taint rule with absent source identities as not run instead of failed (bifrost-dev#15470, fixed by bifrost-dev#15505), and no released Bifrost carries that fix. Changed: python.hardcoded-credentials no longer has an ambiguous hmac.new sink (#417); python.insecure-temporary-file drops the Python 2 os.tempnam and os.tmpnam (#488); python-codeql-quality.comparison-using-is-non-portable drops an unused python-declaration-models capability (#487). Known on Bifrost 0.15.4: python.insecure-temporary-file, overly-permissive-file, polynomial-redos and xml-bomb report not_run (qualified-call-locator-ambiguous) where a typeshed and an authored declaration of the same callable are both active (bifrost-dev#14548, fixed after 0.15.4). Qualification: all 319 open policy fixtures were run with these rules on released Bifrost 0.15.4 with packs 0.16.0 and with packs 0.17.0, and all 319 match. A default run on a plain Python file that imports requests completes all seven new default policies. All other policies, IDs and required capabilities are unchanged from rules 0.17.0. This release does not qualify the full policy set or imply complete analysis.
